messages:
sam: Quick heads-up — noticed a KV cache eviction oscillation under long-context workloads that shows up differently on MI250 vs A100. Memory climbs until we start mass-evicting, then reuse drops and it ramps again. Anyone seen this pattern?

jia: yep saw something similar in the perf run yesterday. MI runs had frequent small evicts while A100 had fewer, larger evicts.

sam: attaching quick perf dump (summarized):

```
KVCacheStats: {alloced: 46GB, used: 44GB, pages: 43000}
evict_cycles: 37
avg_evict_latency_ms: 0.8
reuse_hitrate: 0.12
page_fragmentation_ratio: 0.42
platform: MI250
workload: longctx-16k
```

vs A100:
```
alloced: 48GB, used: 45GB, pages: 28000
avg_evict_latency_ms: 1.4
reuse_hitrate: 0.26
page_fragmentation_ratio: 0.21
platform: A100
```

jia: interesting — MI shows higher fragmentation and lower reuse. could be page-size / segstride differences causing small partial-page allocations.

marcus: did we run the same KV tiling and segment stride on both? sometimes the kernel decides different tiling/kern path on MI because of alignment heuristics.

sam: yes same config, we pinned sequence length dist and batch sizing. Kernel selection log shows MI choosing the "seg-sparse" fallback for some long heads.

anya: @sam can you paste the pager trace from the latest run? need the: page_alloc_pattern + evict_order list.

sam: pasted below (trimmed):

```
[PAGE_TRACE]
alloc: page#1023 len:16 continuous
alloc: page#1024 len:4 fragmented
alloc: page#1025 len:1 fragmented
... repeat pattern every ~1200 allocations
evict_seq: 1023,1026,1024,1030,1025,1027
```

marcus: that interleaving (large contiguous then multiple tiny fragments) would increase fragmentation ratio. If MI's allocator favors small free-list bins differently, we'll see more tiny pages left behind and more frequent evicts.

jia: could also be the KV reuse window logic — if the reuse window uses token-count thresholds that are hit differently due to kernel batching micro-scheduling, you'll get more cache churn on MI.

sam: curious thing: when we flip the policy to prefer LRU (currently we use MRU-ish heuristic to favor recent prefixes), the oscillation frequency drops on MI but reuse hitrate still lags A100 by ~8%.

anja? i meant anya: did we try bumping the eviction batch size? maybe evicting in slightly bigger chunks reduces oscillation.

anya: I ran a quick experiment this morning: evict_batch=128 -> reduces thrash but increases tail latency. Numbers:
- evict_batch=16: tail_p95_evict_ms=1.2 reuse=0.12
- evict_batch=128: tail_p95_evict_ms=4.8 reuse=0.18

marcus: tradeoff expected. We should aim for adaptive batch sizing: increase batch on sustained fragmentation but cap total stall to keep latency SLO.

sam: also saw page-table walk errors (rare) on MI test infra: occasional "stale-owner" warnings during remap. Not sure if it's related but could explain some ghost pages.

jia: do we have repro script? maybe instrument alloc/free ordering with timestamps to see whether remap races correlate with fragmentation spikes.

sam: repro-ish: run longctx-gen.py with synthetic interleaved short+long prompts, seed 42, 30m run. I left traces at s3://redwood-perf/mi250/longctx/1747203000/trace.tar.gz

infra-bot: Perf run finished: job=perf-longctx-mi250-1747203000 status=complete artifacts=s3://redwood-perf/mi250/longctx/1747203000/trace.tar.gz

anya: grabbing artifacts now. Initial grep shows multiple entries of "pt_remap_retry" near the same times as evict_cycles spikes.

marcus: if remap retry -> forces small allocations while waiting, that explains small fragments. The allocator might carve tiny leftover slots. On A100 remap path might be lock-coalesced so fewer retries.

sam: proposal: implement short-term mitigation: 1) coalesce tiny free-list buckets on MI when fragmentation ratio > 0.3, 2) adaptive evict batch sizing based on fragment-run-length, 3) add a short delay/linear backoff on remap retries to reduce micro-allocation bursts.

jia: +1. also add a perf counter to track remap_retry -> fragment correlation per platform.

anya: i'll prototype coalescing patch. expect simple scan every N allocations where we merge contiguous tiny pages. low-risk.

marcus: i'll work on adaptive evict batch sizing and ensure we expose tuning via runtime flags for Dedicated customers.

sam: i'll instrument more detailed page-trace metrics and add dashboard cards (per-route) so we can see this in the Console for affected customers.

jia: small note — verify kernel selection determinism: if MI's compiler/runtime picks a different kernel due to heuristic, we might avoid the fallback path that causes remap retries. Add kernel-selection trace to the perf artifacts.

sam: good call. adding that to the next run. thanks all. :tada:

anya: quick question — what's our rollout plan for the coalesce patch? can we canary on internal Dedicated pool first?

marcus: yes canary internal-green cluster, then 1% internal-prod, monitor reuse & tail latency, then wider.

sam: plan sounds good. I'll create a follow-up ticket with links to artifacts + assigned owners.

infra-bot: Created-ticket: PERF-1287 "kvcache: MI fragmentation coalesce + adaptive-evict" assigned=marcus,jia,anya link=https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/PERF-1287

jia: ack. keeping an eye on dashboards.

sam: thanks. closing thread for now, will update when canary metrics show up.
